Given a dialog $\mathcal{D} = \{u_1, r_1, \dots, u_T, r_T\}$ consisting of $T$ turns, we denote the dialogue context of the $t$ -th turn as $\mathcal{C}_t$ , which encompasses all preceding user utterances and system responses up to that turn, i.e., $\mathcal{C}_t = \{u_1, r_1, \dots, u_{t-1}, r_{t-1}, u_t\}$ . $u_t$ and $r_t$ denote the user utterance and system response of $t$ -th turn, respectively. To adapt to different domain-specific problems, an external knowledge base $\mathcal{K} = \{e_1, e_2, \dots, e_B\}$ is provided as a set of entities. Here, each entity $e_i$ comprises $N$ attribute-value pairs, denoted as $e_i = \{a_1, v_{i,1}, \dots, a_N, v_{i,N}\}$ . End-to-end task-oriented dialogue systems leverage the dialogue context $\mathcal{C}$ and knowledge base $\mathcal{K}$ as input to generate re

sponsetes $\mathcal{R}$

We employ BERT (Devlin et al., 2018) as the encoder of our entity selector and attribute selector and employ T5 (Raffel et al., 2020) to implement the response generator. Our model is trained using AdamW optimizer (Loshchilov and Hutter, 2017) with a batch size of 64. We conduct all experiments on 4 24G NVIDIA RTX 3090 GPUs and select the best checkpoint based on model performance Table 2: Performance on three condensed benchmark datasets. The best scores are in **bold** and the second-best ones are **underlined**.† denotes our model significantly outperforms baselines with $p < 0.05$ under t-test.‡ and § indicates the results cited from Tian et al. (2022) and Raghu et al. (2021), respectively.
